A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AFedPG study and provide readable main text, algorithms, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C. Matching content across pagination changes supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix A report original MuJoCo experiments, including reward curves, timing comparisons, a lookahead ablation, and communication-overhead analysis.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix A retain the original MuJoCo experiments and their empirical reward, timing, ablation, and communication results.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same policy-gradient estimation, normalized server update, and delay-adaptive lookahead procedure. No algorithmic component or objective changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Swimmer-v4, Hopper-v4, Walker2D-v4, and Humanoid-v4 under the same scenarios. Newly mentioned application areas, including diffusion models, cloud computing, and finance, are background examples rather than additional evaluations.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain single-agent PG, synchronous FedPG, the vanilla variant without delay-adaptive lookahead, and A3C. Added literature citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Sections 6.1–6.2 and Appendix A retain the same metrics, agent counts, sample budgets, heterogeneity settings, communication measurements, and Table 3 model and training configurations.

E4.justification: The lookahead ablation and Appendix A.3 analyses of computation heterogeneity, communication overhead, and extended training are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10 runs with seeds 0–9 for the main convergence results and five runs with seeds 0–4 for Figure 8. Averaging, smoothing, and 95% confidence-interval reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The experimental plot images in Figures 3–4 and 6–8 are identical between versions, and the accompanying numerical statements and findings are retained. Figure 8 is enlarged without changing its results.

T1.justification: Definitions 4.1–4.2, Theorems 5.1–5.2, the complexity comparison, and Appendix B's assumptions, lemmas, derivations, and proofs are unchanged after matching corresponding pages.

C1.justification: Section 1 narrows the asserted literature gap from insufficient study of global convergence and time complexity to time complexity. The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same AFedPG novelty, convergence, and speedup claims.

C2.justification: Section 7 newly identifies extension from discounted rewards to average rewards as an open direction. It also elaborates the existing adversarial-worker and second-order-method limitations by connecting them to synchronous robustness and centralized optimal-sample-complexity results.

D1.justification: The implementation descriptions, Table 3 hyperparameters, Appendix A.2 settings, and reproducibility statement remain unchanged, including PyTorch, GAE, policy-network configurations, and A100 hardware. No code or data access information is added.

R1.justification: The cited literature substantially expands across FL fairness, asynchronous multi-model FL, multi-agent learning, diffusion alignment, average-reward RL, and application domains. Several earlier application references are removed or replaced, and Section 1 narrows the literature gap to time complexity. Section 2 and Appendix C retain their central technical comparisons.

P1.justification: The revision makes localized language edits, updates the publication header, adds acknowledgments, and places conclusions before the expanded limitations in Section 7 using inline headings. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is slightly reduced and Figure 8's panels are enlarged while preserving their content. The author block is reformatted, and expanded references cause repagination. All figures and tables are retained.

improvement.justification: V5 clarifies limitations and narrows an overly broad literature-gap statement while retaining the technical and empirical evidence. However, some new citation connections are unclear: Chen et al. (2024a), titled as electricity-price forecasting, supports data-center allocation, while Chen et al. (2024b), titled as agricultural aquifer-recharge control, supports cloud computing. The PDFs do not explain these connections. Clearer scope and these attribution concerns coexist, leaving the net quality effect uncertain.
